content.comment_body: Hello everyone! I am seeking information regarding [article_no] and the communication capacity of an HMI panel. My project requirements are: 10 high-speed counters with individual readings; 10 keys to set counter values; 10 additional keys with various functions ([article_no] and similar); 16 separate displays showing the status of different [product_name] blocks (such as level graphics, block status, etc.). The interface is dynamic and meant for machine control. We already have a similar system running at half the scale for six months. My questions are: 1) Can this amount of data be reliably exchanged between [article_no] and the HMI? 2) Could transmitting too much information cause errors or affect [article_no] workflow? 3) Would sharing information between HMI screens help optimize data exchange? I appreciate any insights from respondents.

analysis.insight_summary: A user wants to know whether the communication between a [product_name] ([article_no]) and an HMI panel can effectively manage numerous dynamic inputs and outputs, without performance issues. They are concerned about reliable data handling and potential workflow errors, and inquire if sharing data between screens could help. The reply is a brief affirmation, lacking technical details.
